description:
Rewrite every unqualified `satisfies:<id>` coverage label in this repository to the container-qualified form `satisfies:<container-short-id>/<id>`, so coverage credit names the container whose criterion it satisfies and nested containers stop crediting each other's same-numbered criteria.

## Background

All 736 `satisfies:` labels in the tracker use the unqualified form. JIT's `label-coverage` rule walks the whole dependency subtree, so an unqualified label credits the same criterion id in every enclosing container. The documentation-overhaul epic had to renumber its stories' criteria (REQ-21..27, REQ-31..40) to avoid false credits. JIT already supports the qualified form and is removing the unqualified one, so this repository must migrate before upgrading to a JIT version without it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed migration script assigns each `satisfies:<id>` label to its owning container, the nearest container in the dependency DAG whose `## Success Criteria` declares that id, and rewrites it to `satisfies:<container-short-id>/<id>`.
- [hard] REQ-02: Labels whose owning container cannot be determined uniquely (no declaring container, or several at the same distance) are listed in a linked record with the reason, and none is rewritten by guess.
- [hard] REQ-03: After migration no unqualified `satisfies:` label remains except those listed under REQ-02, and the coverage verdict of every container is unchanged or strictly more accurate, with each change listed in the linked record.
- [hard] REQ-04: Planning tooling and manifests that emit coverage labels in this repository emit only the qualified form.

## Notes

Coordinate the upgrade with the JIT change that removes the unqualified form; the migration can land before it because the qualified form is already accepted.
title: Migrate satisfies labels to the container-qualified form
